items.sentence: *Can* you *imagine* taking a bite of a steak that was grown in a Petri dish instead of on a farm?
items.pattern: S + Vt + Gerund O + Relative clause (that...)

items.sentence: It *may sound* like something from a sci-fi movie, but these steaks *are* already a reality!
items.pattern: S + Vl+ C + but + S + Vl+ C

items.sentence: Many start-ups *have developed* a special production process in which meat is created by taking animal stem cells, transforming them into primitive fibers, and combining these fibers to form muscle tissue.
items.pattern: S + Vt + O + Relative clause (in which...) + Gerund phrases

items.sentence: The final product, known as lab-grown meat, *is* a thought-provoking recent trend in food science backed by Bill Gates and agricultural giant Cargill.
items.pattern: S + Participial phrase (p.p.) + Vl+ C + Participial phrase (p.p.)

items.sentence: As this technology moves toward mainstream adoption, it *is* important to understand both the promises and the problems with this emerging food source.
items.pattern: Adverbial clause (As...) + It + Vl+ C + Infinitival phrase

items.sentence: Supporters of lab-grown meat *highlight* several substantial benefits that traditional meat production cannot offer.
items.pattern: S + Vt + O + Relative clause (that...)

items.sentence: First, one could *argue* that traditional meat production facilities, such as farms or factories, hardly ever have animals' best interests at heart.
items.pattern: S + Vt + Noun clause (that...)

items.sentence: Growing meat in a laboratory instead *eliminates* the need for slaughterhouses as well as the unethical treatment of animals.
items.pattern: Gerund phrase (S) + Vt + Compound O

items.sentence: In other words, you could *rest assured* that the lab-grown beef patty on your plate didn't come from a cow that had to endure physical or mental torment.
items.pattern: S + Vl+ C + Noun clause (that...) + Relative clause (that...)

items.sentence: Better still, lab-grown meat could *make* meat production more sustainable.
items.pattern: S + Vt + O + C

items.sentence: The raising of livestock needed to fulfill the current global demand for meat actually *takes* a heavy toll on the environment.
items.pattern: S + Participial phrase (p.p.) + Vt (Phrasal verb) + O

items.sentence: According to FAO, it *accounts for* nearly fifteen percent of all greenhouse gas emissions worldwide.
items.pattern: Prepositional phrase + S + Vt (Phrasal verb) + O

items.sentence: Experts *estimate* that by switching to lab-grown meat, emissions could be lowered by up to ninety-six percent.
items.pattern: S + Vt + Noun clause (that...) with Gerund phrase

items.sentence: In addition, many *claim* it won't just be the environment that benefits.
items.pattern: S + Vt + Noun clause + Relative clause (that...)

items.sentence: Scientists can actually *make* lab-grown meat healthier and more nutritious by adding vitamins and minerals that are not always found in natural meat.
items.pattern: S + Vt + O + C + Gerund phrase + Relative clause (that...)

items.sentence: However, despite the evident advantages of this forward-thinking method of food production, there *are* also some concerns surrounding the meat of tomorrow.
items.pattern: Prepositional phrase + There + Vi + S + Participial phrase (pres. p.)

items.sentence: For a start, studies *have shown* that the development of lab-grown meat could actually have far-reaching negative effects in the long term.
items.pattern: S + Vt + Noun clause (that...)

items.sentence: While advocates for lab-grown meat say it can help fight climate change, some research *suggests* that maintaining the infrastructure to grow cell cultures requires significant quantities of energy and leads to substantial gas emissions.
items.pattern: Adverbial clause (While...) + S + Vt + Noun clause (that...) with compound verbs

items.sentence: Another issue to consider *is* whether this type of artificial meat is actually healthy and safe for humans to consume.
items.pattern: S + Infinitival phrase + Vi + Noun clause (whether...)

items.sentence: Although great in theory, lab-grown meat *is* unnatural, similar to genetically modified food.
items.pattern: Elliptical adverbial clause (Although...) + S + Vl+ C

items.sentence: Since the latter is sometimes said to induce allergic reactions or even cause more serious health problems like cancer, some people *are warning* against human-made meat for fear that it might have similar side effects.
items.pattern: Adverbial clause (Since...) + S + Vi + Prepositional phrase + Noun clause (that...)

items.sentence: One final area of concern *is* the actual taste of lab-grown meat.
items.pattern: S + Vl+ C

items.sentence: Without the naturally occurring connective tissue and fat that are present in real meat, lab-grown meat *may be* somewhat *lacking* in taste and texture and thus less appealing to some consumers.
items.pattern: Prepositional phrase with Relative clause (that...) + S + Vl+ C

items.sentence: Therefore, more extensive research *is needed* to determine how the flavor and composition of this new meat might be altered to better suit consumer tastes.
items.pattern: S + Vi + Infinitival phrase + Noun clause (how...)

items.sentence: Whether we welcome it or not, lab-grown meat *is* an innovative product that could have a long-term impact on a global scale.
items.pattern: Adverbial clause (Whether...) + S + Vl+ C + Relative clause (that...)

items.sentence: It *might*, however, *come* at a price.
items.pattern: S + Vi + Prepositional phrase

items.sentence: To ensure that future foods are both sustainable and healthy, it *is* therefore essential for us to conduct more comprehensive research before we jump to any conclusions.
items.pattern: Infinitival phrase with Noun clause + It + Vl+ C + Adverbial clause (before...)

items.sentence: For now, all we can do *is* keep a close eye on this rapidly growing trend.
items.pattern: Prepositional phrase + S with Relative clause + Vi + Bare infinitival C
